question: can row-wise removal remove the banding without blurring time or erasing content?
method: per-row MEDIAN across the 160 columns estimates band(y); the row-constant component is removed, then the frame is rescaled to the capture's median mean luma
limits: the row estimate is contaminated where a subject fills more than half a row's columns -- the filter can partly remove a close subject, which is why the occupied number matters
the empty capture is later and darker; only within-condition comparisons are clean
one capture per condition, no error bars
the reconstruction cannot restore the original absolute luma, only the row-structured part of the change, so the threshold is applied to a reconstructed image
verdict: ROW REMOVAL WORKS AND BEATS THE TEMPORAL MEDIAN. Mode 'divide': empty room 0.06%, occupied 49.30%. The occupied rate STAYS HIGH, which is the thing the temporal median could not do -- at k=5 it fell to 0.48%. No latency, no motion smearing, no frame averaging. Facing vs head-turned gap is 3.12 pp.
